wins.text: Nike Running grew over 20% in Q1, driven by redesigned Vomero, Structure, and Pegasus product lines integrating Air, Flyknit, ZoomX and React X platforms
North America Q1 revenue grew 4%, with wholesale up 11%; running, training, and basketball each delivered double-digit growth
Spring order book is up year-over-year with growth led by sport, and wholesale expected to return to modest growth for fiscal '26
Inventory decreased 2% vs. prior year (units down further) with closeout mix approaching normalized levels in North America and EMEA, on track for healthy marketplace by end of H1 FY26
NIKE Digital repositioning showing early progress: promo days reduced by more than 50 in North America, markdown rates lowered, and full-price share of demand increased

risks.text: Gross margins declined 320 bps to 42.2% due to higher wholesale discounts, factory store discounts, increased product costs including new tariffs, and channel mix headwinds
Annualized gross tariff cost estimate raised to ~$1.5B from ~$1.0B 90 days ago; net FY26 gross margin headwind increased from ~75-120 bps to ~120 bps, with Q2 tariff headwind of 175 bps

Greater China revenue declined 10% (NIKE Digital down 27%, wholesale down 9%, EBIT down 25%); store traffic and in-season sell-through continue to underperform; expected to remain a topline and margin headwind throughout FY26
NIKE Digital organic traffic declining double digits across all geographies; NIKE Direct not expected to return to growth in FY26; Q2 revenue guided down low single digits
Converse under new leadership with marketplace reset underway; revenue and gross margin headwinds from Converse expected to continue throughout FY26

guidance_items.detail: Q2 revenues expected down low single digits, including ~1 point of FX benefit; NIKE Direct not expected to return to growth in FY26
Q2 gross margins expected down ~300-375 bps including 175 bps net headwind from new incremental tariffs; FY26 overall margin outlook moderated vs. prior guidance
Q2 SG&A expected up high single digits driven by acceleration of demand creation investment; FY26 SG&A expected to grow low single digits
Wholesale revenue expected to return to modest growth for FY26; North America to continue leading global recovery
FY26 tax rate expected in low 20% range due to anticipated changes in earnings mix, up from 19.6% prior year

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential pull-forward of consumer demand into back-to-school / August and September trading trends
Timeline and cost of China mono-brand store refresh/pilot program before scaling with partners
Specific milestones and phasing for NIKE Digital to return to profitable growth
